ai.title: Remove local act scripts, fix CI caching
ai.summary: Deleted .github/act scripts (bootstrap-act-config.sh, run-local.sh) and removed `act` npm script. CI workflow updated: renamed 'Restore dependencies' to 'Cache dependencies', added `packages/*/node_modules` to cache paths, added `restore-keys`, and moved env var setup before build. `.github/.gitignore` cleaned of act-specific entries.

eli5.text: The team removed the old way developers ran tests on their own computers and instead improved how the company's automated testing service stores and reuses downloaded dependencies. Now the automated tests run faster and more reliably because they skip re-downloading things they already have. If you looked, you'd see the automated testing setup now covers more of the project's parts and prepares its settings earlier before running.

ai.title: Wrap PostHog flush in try/catch
ai.summary: Wrap `client.flush()` in `try/catch` within `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` to prevent unhandled PostHog network errors. Errors are silently ignored in production, logged only when `DEBUG_DEV_EVENTS` is true.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to send usage data to PostHog, it now quietly handles network errors instead of crashing the whole app. If the data can't be sent, like when you're offline or the server is unreachable, nothing breaks and you won't see any error messages. Only if you're running in a special debugging mode will you be alerted that something went wrong.

ai.title: Fix XML entity parsing and stream handling in saxy
ai.summary: Corrects entity parsing logic in `common/src/util/saxy.ts` to properly handle named and numeric entities without leading ampersands in internal checks, and fixes index offsets for hexadecimal/decimal parsing. Implements `_pendingEntity` state to buffer incomplete entities across stream chunks, ensuring they are resolved in subsequent `_parseChunk` calls or emitted on stream end. Removes previous whitespace trimming logic for top-level tags in favor of immediate entity parsing on text nodes. Updates `npm-app` snapshot tests to reflect corrected output.

eli5.text: When you paste text that contains special symbols written in a shorthand form (like < for a less-than sign), the program now turns all of those symbols into their proper characters correctly, even when the symbols arrive in pieces across multiple chunks. You wouldn't notice a difference in the final text, but while the text is still being processed you might briefly see leftover ampersands if the previous logic left them in. Who is affected today didn't change.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.264
ai.summary: Bumped version from 1.0.263 to 1.0.264 in npm-app/package.json.

eli5.text: The version number was bumped from 1.0.263 to 1.0.264 as part of a routine behind-the-scenes update. This release includes several changes such as switching the analytics reporting to a newer setup in some places. There are no major visible changes for a typical user today.

ai.title: npm-app/src/client.ts: start spinner on prompt continuation
ai.summary: Added `Spinner.get().start()` call in `npm-app/src/client.ts` before sending prompt action via WebSocket. Ensures visual feedback during tool result processing and response wait.

eli5.text: When you send a question to the assistant and it starts working on using tools to help answer it, a small loading spinner now appears on screen while you wait. Previously, this spinner stayed hidden during the moment between when your question was sent and when the assistant began typing its reply. This makes the app feel more responsive and lets you know right away that something is happening behind the scenes. You'd notice this subtle animation showing up earlier in the process whenever the assistant is gathering information or running tools to assist you.

ai.title: Fix tool render spacing
ai.summary: getToolCallString in common/src/constants/tools.ts now concatenates parameters without newlines. Replaced join('\n') with join('') and removed surrounding newlines in the return string. Affects tool call rendering across surfaces using shared constants. Tested in npm-app/src/utils/__tests__/tool-renderers.test.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant shows you a tool call (like running a calculation or fetching data), the parameters used to appear on separate lines with extra blank lines around them, making the display look spread out and loose. Now those parameters are joined together directly and the surrounding blank lines are removed, so tool call output appears compactly and cleanly formatted. You would notice tool call results looking tighter and less spaced out when they are rendered, since the same rendering code is shared across the places that display them. This is a live today visual fix to how tool calls are displayed.

ai.title: Server exits immediately on local
ai.summary: handleShutdown in backend/src/index.ts now calls process.exit(0) when NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT is 'local'. This skips graceful client exit waits, flushing analytics first. Change is internal to the backend server lifecycle.

eli5.text: On your local computer, when you stop the server manually, it now shuts down right away instead of waiting around. When you run the software on your own machine, telling it to quit immediately flushes any pending telemetry data first, then closes without waiting for other connected programs to finish their business. You would notice the server process disappearing faster in your terminal when you press Control+C. This only affects people running the server locally, not the production service.

ai.title: Add timeoutseconds to runterminalcommand
ai.summary: The run_terminal_command tool now accepts a timeout_seconds parameter, defaulting to 30. This replaces the hardcoded MAX_EXECUTION_TIME constant in the PTY and child process implementations, allowing callers to specify custom timeout durations. The change spans backend tool schemas, common constants, and npm-app handlers/utils.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a command in your terminal on your behalf, it now respects a custom time limit you can set instead of a fixed default. If you don't specify one, the command still stops after 30 seconds. You'd notice this if you asked the assistant to run a long command that previously gave up too early; the timeout can now be tuned per command.

ai.title: Fix startup cwd to preserve project root
ai.summary: Startup sequence now separates working directory from project root. `getStartingDirectory` returns object with `cwd` and `shouldSearch` flag to control git root lookup. `setProjectRoot` accepts optional `setCwd` parameter (default false) to prevent unintended directory changes. Affects `npm-app/src/index.ts`, `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts up, it now keeps your current folder as your working directory even when you point it at a project located elsewhere. It separately figures out the project root (for finding config and project files) without changing where your shell is running. If you explicitly give a directory, it no longer searches for a git root inside it. This is live today and affects anyone starting the assistant with a specified project directory.

ai.title: Version 1.0.265
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.265 in `npm-app/package.json`. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: The assistant you use has reached a new numbered release, and this update bundles several fixes that affect how you interact with it. When you ask the assistant to run something that takes time, you'll now see a spinner that shows it's still working while you type follow-up messages, and terminal commands you run through it accept a timeout so they no longer hang indefinitely. It also fixes how shutdown works on a local machine so the tool exits cleanly, corrects the display spacing of tool calls, and preserves your project's starting folder so commands run in the right place.

ai.title: Reduce MAXLENGTH in logger.ts
ai.summary: Lowered `MAX_LENGTH` constant in `backend/src/util/logger.ts` from 100,000 to 70,000 to add buffer for log size limits. Internal adjustment affecting backend logging.

eli5.text: The system now caps how much text it writes in a single log entry, shrinking that ceiling from 100,000 to 70,000 characters. If you were to inspect the logs, you would see entries stop growing sooner before they wrap or roll to a new line. This is an internal safety adjustment on the backend, so it does not change anything you can directly see today; it just keeps future logs from bumping up against size limits the way they did before. Engineers made the same kind of behind-the-scenes cleanup as trimming old scripts, improving cache logic, and making version updates in the same batch.

constants.name: MAX_LENGTH
constants.to: 70_000 // Max total log size is 100k, put some buffer

ai.title: Add usage hint to CLI menu
ai.summary: Adds a console.log instruction to the npm-app menu indicating users can type 'usage' to check remaining credits. This surfaces the usage command in the startup hints within npm-app/src/menu.ts. The change is internal to the CLI presentation layer.

eli5.text: When you start up the assistant in the terminal, you'll now see a new line in the welcome hints that says you can type the word "usage" to check your remaining credits. The program now prints that instruction alongside the other startup tips you already see, like pressing ESC to cancel or typing "init" to auto-configure your project. This change is live today and affects anyone running the assistant from the command line.

ai.title: Allow zero-credit message costs and restructure prompt flow
ai.summary: Changed minimum cost and credits calculation from 1 to 0 in `message-cost-tracker.ts`. Refactored `main-prompt.ts` to move documentation fetching and consecutive message checks out of the initial conditional block. This prevents premature returns and ensures consistent state handling across agent loops.

eli5.text: The assistant will no longer charge a minimum cost for messages that have no value, so free prompts that previously registered a tiny credit cost now register none. Internally, the message handling flow was reorganized so that documentation lookups and checks for consecutive assistant replies happen before deciding whether to stop the loop, preventing premature exits that could skip cleanup steps. If you looked at the logs, you would see prompts completing their full cycle more consistently and zero-cost messages leaving a cleaner trail. This is live now for anyone running the assistant with message cost tracking enabled.

ai.title: Fix extra newline in write file tool
ai.summary:
Updated `getToolCallString` to join parameters with newlines and wrap the resulting string in newlines. Modified `Saxy` parser to ignore stray `
` text nodes when inside a single root tag. Adjusted `Client` prompt output to prepend the newline to the styled label. Affects `common/src/constants/tools.ts`, `common/src/util/saxy.ts`, and `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant to write a file, the displayed command now shows each parameter on its own line instead of all run together, making it easier to read. The text parser that breaks up responses was also taught to ignore stray blank lines that used to sneak in between the parts, which stopped extra empty lines from appearing in your output. This is live today for anyone using the CodeBuff tool to write files or run commands.
